description: Machine-friendly NL2SQL guide for the M3 inventory module. Covers main tables, business synonyms, join hints, key relations, and query-generation rules.

join_hints.name: inventory_request_to_transfer_flow
join_hints.description: Flow from material requests to stock transfers.

join_hints.name: inventory_request_to_receipt_flow
join_hints.description: Flow from material requests to stock receipts.

join_hints.name: transfer_to_receipt_flow
join_hints.description: Flow from stock transfers to stock receipts.

join_hints.name: stock_opname_adjustment_flow
join_hints.description: Flow from stock opname to stock transactions or balance adjustments.

join_hints.name: opening_balance_inventory_flow
join_hints.description: Relationship from inventory opening-balance headers to opening-balance details.

detail_lineage_keys.name: ts_detail_to_mr
detail_lineage_keys.business_meaning: Trace a transfer-stock line back to the originating material request.

detail_lineage_keys.name: rs_detail_to_mr
detail_lineage_keys.business_meaning: Trace a receive-stock line back to the originating material request.

detail_lineage_keys.name: rs_detail_to_ts
detail_lineage_keys.business_meaning: Trace a receive-stock line back to the originating stock transfer.

detail_lineage_keys.name: sa_detail_to_sp
detail_lineage_keys.business_meaning: Trace a stock-adjustment line back to the originating stock opname.

important_rules: Use header tables for document numbers, dates, warehouses, and inventory transaction status.
Use detail tables for items, quantities, units, latest stock values, and realization progress.
For inventory-flow tracing, start from detail tables so the stage-to-stage flow stays accurate.
For daily-check questions, distinguish between `m3_dc_detail` and `m3_dc_check` depending on whether the user needs unit data or checklist data.
Use `m3_sp` and `m3_sa` for stock-opname and stock-adjustment analytics.
Use `m1_item` for general items and `m1_item_hauling` for hauling daily-check context.
Avoid `custom*` fields unless the user or report explicitly requires them.

query_patterns.name: document_summary
query_patterns.pattern: Use header tables such as `m3_mr`, `m3_ts`, `m3_rs`, `m3_sp`, or `m3_ib` for transaction numbers, dates, warehouses, and statuses.

query_patterns.name: document_items
query_patterns.pattern: Join header to detail, for example `m3_ts -> m3_ts_detail` or `m3_ib -> m3_ib_detail`.

query_patterns.name: inventory_flow_trace
query_patterns.description: Trace inventory flow from request to transfer and receipt.
query_patterns.pattern: Start from detail tables: `MR -> MR_DETAIL -> TS_DETAIL -> RS_DETAIL`.

query_patterns.name: stock_opname_trace
query_patterns.description: Trace stock opname to adjustment transactions.

caution_areas: Questions that mix MR, TS, and RS only at header level without detail context.
Stock-opname questions that actually require progress tables.
Daily-check questions that need a distinction between checklist data and operational detail.
History questions that mix active tables and history tables.
